# the contributor audit: actual-volume counterexample to the sum of ordinary maxima

Source: `candidate 0549d69dcd95de34`.


`2^(-n) sum A(K_z)`. It does not falsify OC.

## Exact bodies and normalization

For D, reflection in the displayed center interchanges each coordinate
bound and interchanges the two total-sum bounds. Every center inequality
is strict. At fixed `S=x2+...+x8`, intersecting the two x1 intervals gives
exact length `11/18-|S-7/18|`, positive over the entire base cube.
The eight-dimensional simplex integral and inclusion-exclusion prove
the recorded expectation and volume. This uses no numerical quadrature.

The diagonal factor q scales volume linearly, so its rational definition
indeed gives `|C|=2 Gamma V`. Both contraction factors lie in (0,1),
and every coordinate bound used later follows from the actual contraction
of D. The small cube A has volume a, and the actual midpoint sum lies
strictly under the sum facet of B because `lambda+4 epsilon=123/125`.
Nonnegative coordinates and this sum bound establish full midpoint
containment. The three-fiber hull has exactly those sections at its only
integer bases and is a full-dimensional convex body.

Central symmetry gives the two endpoint ordinary maxima exactly, and
the simplex theorem gives the middle maximum. Thus the proposed stronger
target is exactly `Gamma V+a/4`, while the original total volume is
`(1+2 Gamma)V+a`. These quantities are not interchanged.

## All thirteen cap incidences

For the two costly barycentric caps, the tilt -2z includes the entire
small cube and strictly excludes C. For each of the other seven caps,
the chosen common affine cutoff makes the maximum on both endpoints
equal to `epsilon/2+lambda/9`; the displayed strict gap places it below
the middle threshold. Therefore all nine middle cap volumes are the
actual simplex trace volumes plus precisely the specified endpoint mass.
The barycentric thresholds sum to one, so the nine closed traces cover
every middle candidate, including every boundary point.

The two cuts at each endpoint have half its actual volume and strictly
exclude both other fibers by the stated finite integer tilts. They cover
every endpoint candidate. All caps are full ambient closed halfspaces.
Their covering role is an upper bound on maximal depth and does not rely
on minimizing-cap attainment.

## Exact strict budget

The derivative identity `8(8/9)^7=9 Gamma` gives the common first-order
increment `2 alpha/9`. On the required unit interval the second derivative
of the eighth power is at most 56, and both displacement coefficients
are less than 1/3. Thus each middle mass is at most

    Gamma V + 2a/9 + 28a^2/(9V).

Since `alpha=a/V<1/1000`, the gap to `Gamma V+a/4` exceeds
`(37/1500)a`. Endpoint budgets are smaller as well. This is a fixed,
strict, rational finite-cover certificate for the actual-volume failure.

At the actual centroid of C, its own contribution `Gamma V` exceeds
OC's `Gamma[(1+2 Gamma)V+a]/2`, since `alpha<1-2 Gamma`. Thus the source
has a separate explicit OC certificate and is not presented as a
counterexample to the target goal.

The root reran `supporting computation verify_actual_sum_own_maximal_depth_counterexample.py`
under plain Python: PASS. The exact verifier is a check on the displayed
analytic certificate, not a substitute for it.
